summary: Citizenship-for-money schemes that ended before 2015, outside the jurisdictions already covered. Ireland (1988-1998) is well documented in official Dáil records: 183 people (107 investors) naturalised, over IR£90-100m invested, with a damning 1998 internal review. Comoros (2008-2016) has IMF figures on revenue (but inconsistent across reports) and serious press coverage of a parliamentary inquiry and a 2022 treason conviction; the inquiry report and law text were not obtained. Tonga rests on press reports only; Belize and St Vincent rest mainly on US State Department reports. Nauru events reuse nru-citizen-investor from new-programmes.json.

observations.quote: Selon les données recueillies par la commission parlementaire, 47.950 passeports ont été émis dans le cadre de ce programme.
observations.notes: Exact count from the commission data as reported by AFP.

observations.quote: more than 1,000 people whose place of birth was listed as in Iran bought Comoros passports between 2008 and 2017
observations.notes: Buyers born in Iran, from a passport database reviewed by Reuters; 'more than'. Persons, not passports, strictly.

observations.quote: In April 2015, a Moroni court ruled that Comoro Gulf Holding owed the state USD $16m from the economic citizenship programme
observations.notes: Court ruling reported by the Guardian; judgment not seen.

observations.quote: Le procureur avait avancé la somme d'1,8 milliard d'euros détournés, soit davantage que le PIB de l'archipel.
observations.notes: Prosecutor's figure at trial, as reported by RFI. Defence said no trace of the money was found. Far above the commission's estimates.

program_terms.quote: involves a substantial investment by the applicant
program_terms.notes: No minimum amount in the published Statement of Intent; required two years' residence with at least 60 days present, a residence in the State, and a job-creating project. The review found most early cases did not meet these conditions.

program_terms.quote: an investment of about £500,000 would be required
program_terms.notes: Internal Department of Justice working rule, not a Government decision; the Government left each case to the Minister's discretion. Start date not stated.

program_terms.location: Appendix C, Terms of Reference (Department of Justice, October 1994), criterion (b)
program_terms.quote: The level of investment must involve a net contribution of at least £1 million per applicant.
program_terms.notes: Investment (equity or a 7-year low-interest loan to the firm) held at least 5 years; residence bought and kept 5 years; 60 days in the State in the 2 years after naturalisation. Announced in the Dáil 25 Oct 1994 (irl-dail-pq-1994-10-25).

program_terms.quote: the level of investment must involve a net contribution of at least £1 million per applicant
program_terms.notes: Same rule as above, as read into the record on 25 Oct 1994.

program_terms.quote: two individuals purchased economic citizenships from Belize for $25,000 apiece
program_terms.notes: Price actually paid by two buyers in December 2001, as reported by the US State Department; printed with '$' only (presumably US dollars). Not a published official schedule.

program_terms.quote: For $10,000, someone who was otherwise stateless could become a Tongan Protected Person
program_terms.notes: Travel document only; no right to enter or settle in Tonga. Currency '$' only. Dates not given.

program_terms.quote: a new Tongan passport went on sale for $20,000 (or $35,000 for a family of four)
program_terms.notes: Full Tongan nationality with right to settle. Currency '$' only.

program_terms.quote: a new Tongan passport went on sale for $20,000 (or $35,000 for a family of four)

program_terms.applies_to: 4,000 Bidoon families (bulk deal with the UAE)
program_terms.quote: The first phase of the scheme, under Sambi, who was in power from 2006 to 2011, was meant to earn Comoros $200 million in return for giving citizenship to 4,000 stateless families.
program_terms.notes: Total for the whole deal, not per person. Emirati officials told the commission they paid in full; little trace was found in public accounts.

program_terms.quote: A new agreement set the price of a passport at 4,600 euros, and said a minimum of 5,000 passports would be issued.
program_terms.notes: Terms of the 2011 agreement under President Dhoinine, as reported by Reuters from the commission report.

program_terms.quote: the government grants citizenship (in exchange for KMF 1 million; about US$3,000) to foreigners willing to make large investments in Comoros
program_terms.notes: IMF's description. The same definition appears in IMF Country Report 13/33 (footnote 5). Much lower than the per-passport prices reported elsewhere, which suggests it is the official fee, not what buyers paid.

program_terms.quote: Most of the price paid for the passports -- between 25,000 and 200,000 euros -- was stolen
program_terms.notes: Range of prices paid, per the parliamentary report as read by AFP. Upper end EUR 200,000.

events.title: Government approves naturalisation for anyone prepared to invest
events.description: The review says the Government, in April 1989, approved a large group of applications and decided future applications from investors should also be approved; a Statement of Intent was then given to enquirers.
events.quote: The Government decided that the applications should be approved and, furthermore, so should future applications for anybody who was prepared to invest in the State.

events.title: Advisory group terms of reference set a IR£1 million minimum
events.description: Minister announces Government-approved terms of reference: IR£1m net investment per applicant, Forfás monitoring, police certificates; the scheme to be put on a statutory basis (never done).
events.quote: the level of investment must involve a net contribution of at least £1 million per applicant

events.title: No new applications accepted pending legislation
events.description: Government decides to stop accepting new applications until specific legislation is in place; existing applications continue.
events.quote: On 4 September 1996 the Government decided that no new applications should be accepted pending the introduction of specific legislation

events.title: Minister announces formal end of the scheme
events.description: Press release: formal ending of the Investment Based Naturalisation Scheme; outstanding cases on hand to be processed under the 1994 procedure.
events.location: Appendix F, press release dated 20 April 1998
events.quote: today announced the formal ending of the Investment Based Naturalisation Scheme

events.title: Department of Justice review published in the Dáil record
events.description: Minister places the substance of the Feb 1998 review and its statistics in the Official Report. It finds regulation of the scheme 'very difficult' and that it should not be re-established.
events.quote: The Minister is of the view that the Scheme, as constituted, should not be re-established.

events.title: Minister finds 11 passports granted in 1990 were 'irregular and unusual'
events.description: After examining the file (also held by the Moriarty Tribunal), the Minister tells the Dáil that 11 passports and naturalisations were granted bypassing usual formalities; passports were prepared before applications were complete. He also confirms the Review Group report was published in August 2002.
events.quote: the 11 passports and naturalisations in question were granted in a manner which was, even by the lax standards that have frequently characterised the operation of the scheme in question, irregular and unusual

events.title: Citizenship Act 2004 rules out any future investment scheme
events.description: Section 10 narrows 'Irish associations' to blood, affinity or adoption links, which the Minister said puts such schemes beyond possibility.
events.quote: That undertaking has been fulfilled by the provisions of section 10 of the Bill.

events.title: Two economic citizens tied to a terrorist group refused US visas
events.description: US embassy in Belize refused visas to two people who had just bought Belizean economic citizenship; the State Department says they were members of a proscribed Middle Eastern terrorist group.
events.quote: They were denied entry visas by the consular staff of the American embassy in Belize because the two applicants were members of a proscribed Middle Eastern terrorist group.

events.title: Belize announces end of economic citizenship sales
events.description: According to the US State Department, the Government of Belize announced it would cease selling economic citizenships in January 2002. A 2020 academic report also dates the end to 2002.
events.quote: The government of Belize subsequently announced that it would cease selling economic citizenships in January 2002.

events.title: Belize marked as not selling economic citizenship (US INCSR 2002 table)
events.description: The 2002 offshore financial services table marks Belize 'N' in the 'Sells Economic Citizenship' column (2001 table: 'S', suspended or ceased).
events.quote: Sells Economic Citizenship

events.title: US lists jurisdictions actively selling economic citizenship
events.description: State Department names five Caribbean sellers (Belize, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts/Nevis, St Vincent and the Grenadines) and Nauru in the Pacific.
events.quote: Currently five Caribbean Basin OFCs are actively selling economic citizenships: Belize, Dominica, Grenada, St. Kitts/Nevis and St. Vincent and the Grenadines. In the Pacific region, economic citizenships are for sale in Nauru.

events.title: St Vincent revokes economic citizenship programme
events.description: SVG revoked the programme that provided the legal basis to sell citizenship and passports; no passports had been issued.
events.location: St. Vincent and the Grenadines country section
events.quote: In April 2001 SVG revoked its economic citizenship program, which provided the legal basis to sell SVG citizenship and passports; however, no passports had been issued.

events.title: US: Nauru sells 'improperly controlled' economic citizenships
events.description: INCSR 2001 says that in the Pacific, Nauru sells improperly controlled economic citizenships.
events.quote: In the Pacific region, Nauru sells improperly controlled economic citizenships.

events.title: Nauru still marked as selling economic citizenship (INCSR 2003 table)
events.description: The 2003 offshore financial centers table still marks Nauru 'Y' for selling economic citizenship.
events.quote: Sells Economic Citizenship

events.title: Tonga begins selling passports (press accounts)
events.description: CNN dates the sales from 1983, proposed by Hong Kong businessman George Chen; proceeds to the Tonga Trust Fund at Bank of America, San Francisco.
events.quote: Between 1983 and 1991 over 5,000 were sold raising around $30 million.

events.title: US says Tonga still sells economic citizenship
events.description: The State Department's 2000 report says Tonga sells economic citizenship, which contradicts press accounts that sales ended in 1991.
events.quote: Tonga also sells economic citizenship.

events.title: Government admits trust fund money lost
events.description: Tonga says the Tonga Trust Fund lost 50 million pa'anga through schemes promoted by the King's court jester and that it has started legal action.
events.quote: In a statement the government said its Tonga Trust Fund had begun legal proceedings to recover the money.

events.title: Tonga Trust Fund sues Bogdonoff and others in San Francisco
events.description: Suit for fraud and negligence over the losses in Millennium Asset Management and alleged secret commissions.
events.quote: the suit filed in San Francisco in June 2002

events.title: Out-of-court settlement
events.description: Defendants pay about US$0.9-1m up front without admitting liability. Two Tongan ministers had resigned over the affair.
events.quote: Tonga has settled a long-running lawsuit against its American court jester

events.title: Parliament rejects economic citizenship bill
events.description: In a heated July 2008 session the assembly rejected the bill, calling it an auction of Comorian nationality.
events.quote: In a heated session of debate in July 2008, the parliament rejected a proposed “economic citizenship” bill

events.title: Economic citizenship law signed
events.description: After a Gulf trip for MPs organised by Comoro Gulf Holding, the bill passed in November 2008 amid a walkout and was signed by President Sambi.
events.quote: On November 27, 2008, amidst continuing public discontent, the bill was signed into law by President Sambi.

events.title: Kuwait official says Bidun could get Comoros citizenship
events.description: Kuwaiti interior ministry official says stateless Bidun would get special applications for Comoros economic citizenship.
events.quote: Tens of thousands of stateless people in Kuwait - known as Bidun - could be offered citizenship of the Comoros islands off Africa, an official says.

events.title: Sales suspended under President Azali
events.description: The Azali government says it has suspended citizenship sales since coming to power in May 2016.
events.quote: The current Comoros government, led by President Azali Assoumani, has said it has suspended citizenship sales since coming to power in May 2016.

events.title: Parliamentary commission of inquiry set up
events.description: Cross-party commission set up to investigate the programme; report completed December 2017 but not publicly released.
events.quote: The report, produced by a parliamentary commission set up in June 2017

events.title: Government gives first official tally: nearly 52,000 sold
events.description: Foreign minister says most passports bought outside the official programme went to people of Iranian origin.
events.quote: Comoros has sold citizenship to nearly 52,000 foreigners since 2009

events.title: Leaked inquiry report: law passed unlawfully, 'mafia' networks, missing revenue
events.description: The commission found the law was changed in a session that violated procedure and the promulgated text lacks proper signatures; it named ex-presidents Sambi and Dhoinine as suspects.
events.quote: The cross-party commission found that the law allowing the sale of citizenship was changed during a parliamentary session that violated its own procedures.

events.title: Ex-president Sambi charged
events.description: Sambi formally charged with corruption and embezzlement of public funds over the passport scheme, and detained.
events.quote: Comoros ex-president Ahmed Abdallah Mohamed Sambi has been formally charged with corruption and embezzling public funds in connection with a scheme to sell his country’s passports

events.title: High treason trial opens at the State Security Court
events.description: Sambi tried before the Cour de sûreté de l'État; the investigating judge had requalified the charges as high treason.
events.quote: a comparu lundi devant la Cour de sûreté de l'État à Moroni pour « haute trahison »

events.title: Sambi sentenced to life; 11 co-accused convicted
events.description: State Security Court (no appeal possible) gives Sambi life imprisonment for high treason; ex-vice president Mohamed Ali Soilihi 20 years in absentia; prosecutor had alleged EUR 1.8bn diverted. Defence called the trial political; UN body had called his pre-trial detention arbitrary.
events.quote: Les peines vont de deux ans de prison avec sursis à la perpétuité, pour l'ancien président, reconnu coupable de « haute trahison ».

programs.name: Investment-based naturalisation scheme ('passports for investment')
programs.notes: No law of its own: the Minister for Justice used the discretion in section 16 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 1956 (as amended 1986) to waive the residence condition for investors, treating the investment as 'Irish associations'. Government approved the approach in April 1989, but the Department's review counts naturalisations from 1988 (and the 2002 Minister said it was introduced in 1988; the 2000 Minister said 1989). Applicant, spouse and children under 18 could be included. Before 1994 the Department's working rule was about IR£500,000; from October 1994 an advisory group applied a minimum net investment of IR£1 million per applicant, a residence to be kept 5 years and 60 days' presence in the 2 years after naturalisation. New applications stopped on 4 Sep 1996; the scheme was formally ended on 20 Apr 1998, but cases already accepted were processed later (naturalisations recorded up to 2004). Section 10 of the Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 2004 removed the legal basis. Totals given to the Dáil: 143 persons by Feb 1998; 183 persons (107 investors) in the final count. The Department's 1998 review found most early cases did not meet the published conditions (e.g. good-character evidence in 17 of 66).

programs.name: Belize economic citizenship programme
programs.notes: Citizenship sold to 'economic citizens' under the Belize Nationality Act; the Act still mentions dependants of an 'economic citizen'. The US State Department listed Belize as selling economic citizenship in 2000 and 2001, at $25,000 per person (currency not stated), and reported that Belize announced it would stop in January 2002 after two buyers linked to a terrorist group were refused US visas. Start date, legal text and numbers sold not found.

programs.name: St Vincent and the Grenadines economic citizenship programme (2000-2001)
programs.notes: Legislative framework created around 2000; the government projected about US$4.5 million in 2000 from passport sales. Revoked in April 2001; the US State Department says no passports had been issued. Only source found: US INCSR.

programs.name: Tonga passport and citizenship sales (Tongan Protected Person passports and naturalisation), proceeds held in the Tonga Trust Fund
programs.notes: Proposed to the King by Hong Kong businessman George Chen. First 'Tongan Protected Person' passports (travel document, no right to live in Tonga), later full Tongan nationality. Buyers were mostly Hong Kong Chinese; Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos were among them. Press accounts give 1983-1991, over 5,000 sold and about $30 million raised (currency not stated); the US State Department still said Tonga sold economic citizenship in 2000. The money was held in the Tonga Trust Fund at Bank of America, San Francisco; from 1999 it was managed on the advice of the King's 'court jester' Jesse Bogdonoff and largely lost in Millennium Asset Management (viatical insurance). Tonga sued in San Francisco in June 2002 and settled in February 2004. No official Tongan document found.

programs.name: Comoros economic citizenship programme (citoyenneté économique)
programs.notes: Law on economic citizenship signed by President Sambi on 27 Nov 2008 after an earlier rejection (July 2008); a parliamentary inquiry later found the vote broke procedure. Mainly bulk sales to the UAE (and talks with Kuwait) to document stateless Bidoon, who did not move to Comoros; an initial deal of $200m for 4,000 families, then (2011) EUR 4,600 per passport with a minimum of 5,000. The IMF describes it as citizenship for KMF 1 million (about US$3,000) per person, with receipts routed via the Banque de France. Proceeds were large relative to GDP (IMF: about 3-4.5% in 2012 in 2013 reports, over 6% in the 2015 report). Passports were also sold outside the official channel, including to Iranians. Suspended after President Azali took office in May 2016. A parliamentary commission (set up June 2017, report Dec 2017) estimated missing revenue of $100m (Reuters) or $971m (AFP); the State Security Court sentenced ex-president Sambi to life for 'high treason' on 28 Nov 2022. Official law text and commission report not obtained.

new_indicators.name: Losses of a CBI-financed fund
new_indicators.definition: Amount of a fund financed by citizenship sales reported lost, written off or missing (e.g. Tonga Trust Fund investment losses)
new_indicators.notes: Stock-like, usually cumulative to a date; often only press figures

new_indicators.name: Money recovered for a CBI-financed fund
new_indicators.definition: Amounts recovered through settlements or court awards for losses of a fund financed by citizenship sales

new_indicators.name: CBI revenue missing or diverted
new_indicators.definition: Estimated CBI money that should have reached the state but did not (diverted, embezzled or never transferred), as estimated by an inquiry, prosecutor or auditor
new_indicators.notes: Estimates by inquiries differ hugely; always check the source's method

new_indicators.name: Court award relating to CBI money
new_indicators.definition: Amount a court orders a party to pay the state in connection with CBI proceeds

gaps: Ireland: the 2002 Report of the Review Group on Investment Based Naturalisation (published 4 Aug 2002, copies in the Oireachtas Library) was not found online; its para 2.14 gives the IR£100m figure. Year-by-year naturalisations exist only for 1992-1994. Moriarty Tribunal material on the 11 passports not read.
Ireland: oireachtas.ie pages sit behind an AWS CAPTCHA; all debates were taken from the official open-data XML instead.

Tonga: no official Tongan document (Nationality Act amendments of the 1980s-1991, Legislative Assembly records, Supreme Court cases on PacLII, trust fund accounts) - PacLII and the Tonga AGO site blocked automated access. All numbers are press reports with '$' of unclear currency; the end date of sales is contradictory (press: 1991; US State Dept: still selling in 2000).
Belize: no copy of the Belize Nationality Act provisions on economic citizenship, no start date, price schedule or numbers sold; only US State Department reports and an academic summary.

Comoros: Law No. 08-014 of 27 Nov 2008 on economic citizenship, the parliamentary commission report (Dec 2017) and the State Security Court judgment (Nov 2022) were not obtained. Kiwan's sentence and other co-accused's sentences not confirmed from a source read. IMF 2010-2011 programme reviews (with yearly ECP outturns) not located because the IMF eLibrary bot check throttled the search; IMF PDFs could not be downloaded (HTML full text stored instead).

Comoros: revenue figures conflict - IMF 2013 report says about 3% of GDP (tables) and 4.5% (text) for 2012, the 2015 report says over 6%; missing-money estimates range from $100m (Reuters) to $971m (AFP) to EUR 1.8bn (prosecutor).

Marshall Islands, Samoa and Cape Verde: nothing found in an official or serious source within this pass (the web-search budget ran out); no records created. Cape Verde's programme is post-2015 and out of scope.
Nauru: only US State Department mentions (selling 2000-2003); no prices, numbers, start or end date.
leads: Ireland Review Group report 2002: ask the Oireachtas Library or Department of Justice; Moriarty Tribunal Report Part 1 (2006) for the 1990 passports case.
Ireland: Dáil written answers 1997-1998 (many questions on the scheme) via the Oireachtas API by date: https://api.oireachtas.ie/v1/debates?chamber=dail&date_start=1998-01-01&date_end=1998-06-30

Tonga: PacLII Tonga Supreme Court and legislation pages (http://www.paclii.org/to/), e.g. challenges to the 1991 nationality amendments; Tonga Trust Fund v. Bogdonoff, San Francisco Superior Court (2002-2004).

Comoros: IMF ECF review reports 2010-2011 (IMF eLibrary, CR series 2010-2012) for ECP outturns; African Development Bank Comoros reports for the $33.6m 2012 figure; US cable 09ANTANANARIVO2 (archive.org: https://ia800203.us.archive.org/14/items/09ANTANANARIVO2/09ANTANANARIVO2.pdf - download timed out).

Comoros: OCCRP Semlex investigation https://www.occrp.org/en/biometric-bribery-semlex/the-optimist-without-borders-inside-the-semlex-ceos-empire-of-influence ; Reuters 'How to make millions selling passports to Africa' http://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/africa-passports-karaziwan/ (2,800 diplomatic passports finding).
Belize: Jeff Veteto, 'The Alienability of Allegiance', The International Lawyer 48(1), 2014, p. 93 (JSTOR 24889899); Belize Nationality Act Cap. 161 (Revised Edition).
IMF reports found but not read for this topic: Tonga CR 09/292 and 10/112, Marshall Islands CR 10/51, Samoa CR 10/46, Belize CR 09/69 and 11/18.
